extraction.name: MVBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive Multi-modal Video understanding Benchmark covering 20 challenging temporal-related video tasks ranging from perception to cognition that cannot be effectively solved with a single frame. It consists of multiple-choice QA pairs automatically converted from 11 public video datasets to evaluate MLLMs.
extraction.creator: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Videos were collected from 11 existing public video datasets (STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA) covering diverse scenes, first-person and third-person perspectives, and indoor and outdoor environments. Videos were filtered based on video diversity, temporal sensitivity, and question difficulty.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 11 public video datasets: STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Short clips with negligible motions and extremely long videos with complicated contexts were eliminated, retaining intermediate durations primarily from 5s to 35s. For STAR, start and end points were randomly shifted. For CLEVRER, questions necessitating more than 10 conditions were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were auto-generated into multiple-choice QA format using ChatGPT and ground-truth video annotations. Questions were generated via ChatGPT based on task definitions. Answer options were constructed via template-based candidates or LLM-based generation. 3 to 5 options were randomly sampled and shuffled, and LLMs were used to check and equalize option length to avoid answer leakage. Each of the 20 tasks contains 200 QA pairs, totaling 4,000 multiple-choice QA pairs.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Addressed answer length bias where longer options tend to be correct by ensuring options are of similar and reasonable lengths using LLMs. Multiple-choice format based on ground truth annotations was chosen over open-ended generation to avoid the biased scoring of LLMs or user studies.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Visual information alone may not be sufficient for complex cognition tasks like episodic reasoning and egocentric navigation, which benefit from additional modalities like speech subtitles, depth, and audio. Models also exhibit low performance in position, count, and character-related tasks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating temporal understanding and comprehension capabilities of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
